fields.Front: What is the main practical difference between type and interface in TypeScript for object shapes?
fields.Back: interfaces can be reopened and merged via declaration merging; type aliases cannot be merged but can express unions, intersections, and other non-object types that interface can't.

What is the key difference between unknown and any in TypeScript?
fields.Back: any disables type checking entirely; unknown is type-safe — you must narrow it (e.g. with a type guard) before you can use it as anything specific.

fields.Front: How do you narrow a variable value: unknown to a string using typeof?
How do you code a custom type guard function isAdmin that narrows a User to an Admin?
fields.Back:
function isAdmin(user: User): user is Admin {
  return (user as Admin).permissions !== undefined;
}

fields.Front: What does the utility type Partial<T> do?
fields.Back: It produces a type identical to T but with every property made optional.

What is a key gotcha of numeric TypeScript enums compared to string enums?
fields.Back: Numeric enums are reverse-mapped (both name-to-value and value-to-name exist), and any number is structurally assignable to them, so invalid numeric values can slip through type checking. String enums don't have this problem.

fields.Front: What does 'structural typing' mean in TypeScript?
fields.Back: Type compatibility is based on the shape (members) a type has, not on its declared name — two differently-named types with the same members are interchangeable.

fields.Front: What does enabling "strict": true in tsconfig.json do?
fields.Back: It turns on a bundle of stricter checks, including strictNullChecks, noImplicitAny, and strict function types, catching many more potential bugs at compile time.

fields.Front: How do you code a discriminated union for a Shape that is either a Circle or a Square, keyed on a kind field?
fields.Back:
type Shape =
  | { kind: 'circle'; radius: number }
  | { kind: 'square'; side: number };

function area(s: Shape) {
  return s.kind === 'circle' ? Math.PI * s.radius ** 2 : s.side ** 2;
}

fields.Front: How do you type the props of a reusable, accessible UI component (e.g. for a WCAG-compliant button library) so it requires an aria-label when there's no visible text child?
fields.Back:
type ButtonProps =
  | { children: string; 'aria-label'?: string }
  | { children?: never; 'aria-label': string };

fields.Front: How do you code a generic React component's props type ListProps<T> that takes an array of items and a render function?
fields.Back:
type ListProps = {
  items: T[];
  renderItem: (item: T) => JSX.Element;
};

function List({ items, renderItem }: ListProps) {
  return 
    {items.map(renderItem)}
;
}

fields.Front: What does the readonly modifier do on a TypeScript interface property?
fields.Back: It prevents that property from being reassigned after the object is created, catching accidental mutation at compile time (it does not deep-freeze the object).

fields.Front: What does appending as const to an array or object literal do to its inferred type?
fields.Back: It infers the narrowest possible literal types and makes all properties readonly, instead of widening to general types like string[].

fields.Front: What does the never type represent in TypeScript, and where does it commonly show up?
fields.Back: A type with no possible values — it shows up as the return type of a function that always throws, and is useful for exhaustiveness checks in a switch over a union.

fields.Front: How do you write an exhaustiveness check in a switch over a discriminated union so TypeScript errors if a new variant is added later?
fields.Back:
default: {
  const _exhaustive: never = s;
  throw new Error('Unhandled shape');
}

fields.Text: A {{c1::union}} type (A | B) means a value is A or B; an {{c2::intersection}} type (A & B) means a value must satisfy both A and B at once.
